Gradually whisk in the whole milk, a little at a time, until completely smooth with no lumps. 4. Cook the milk mixture: Place the saucepan with the milk mixture over medium heat. Remove the pan from the oven and let the bites rest in the muffin tin for 3–4 minutes to firm up and finish steaming inside. Ingredients: 3/4 cup whole milk (warm, about 110°F); 2 tsp active dry yeast; 1/4 cup granulated sugar; 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour (plus 2–4 tbsp extra as needed); 1/2 tsp fine sea salt; 1 tsp ground cardamom; 1 large egg (room temperature); 4 tbsp unsalted butter (softened); 4 tbsp unsalted butter (very soft); 1/2 cup light brown sugar (packed); 1 1/2 tbsp ground cinnamon; 1/2 tsp ground cardamom; 1/4 tsp fine sea salt; 1/3 cup finely chopped pistachios (unsalted, shelled); 2 tbsp unsalted butter (melted, for greasing); 2 tbsp granulated sugar (for dusting cups); 1 cup powdered sugar (sifted); 2 tbsp fresh orange juice (plus 1–2 tsp more as needed); 1 tsp finely grated orange zest; 1/2 tsp rose water (or to taste; start small); 1 tsp unsalted butter (melted); Pinch fine sea salt; 2 tbsp finely chopped pistachios; Extra orange zest
Method: 1. Prepare the dough 2. Warm the milk to about 110°F — warm to the touch, not hot. In a small bowl, stir together warm milk, yeast, and 1 tbsp of the granulated sugar. Let sit 5–10 minutes until foamy on top. 3. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together 2 1/4 cups flour, remaining granulated sugar, salt, and ground cardamom. 4. Add the foamy yeast mixture and the egg to the dry ingredients. Stir with a wooden spoon until a shaggy dough forms. 5. Add the softened 4 tbsp butter and work it into the dough. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead 7–9 minutes, adding 1–3 tbsp additional flour only as needed, until the dough is smooth, elastic, and just slightly tacky but not sticky. 6. Shape into a ball, place in a lightly greased bowl, cover tightly, and let rise in a warm spot until doubled, about 1 hour. 7. Prepare the muffin pan 8. While the dough rises, thoroughly brush all 12 wells of a standard muffin tin with the 2 tbsp melted butter, making sure to coat the sides and bottom of each cup. 9. Sprinkle about 1/2 tsp granulated sugar into each greased well, rotating and tapping so the sugar lightly coats the bottom and lower sides. This sugared butter layer helps the spirals caramelize and set into a firm, molded shape that releases cleanly. 10. Make the filling 11. In a small bowl, mix the very soft 4 tbsp butter, brown sugar, cinnamon, cardamom, and salt until it forms a smooth, spreadable paste. 12. Stir in the finely chopped pistachios. Set aside at room temperature (you want it soft, not chilled). 13. Shape the spiral bites 14. Punch down the risen dough gently to deflate. Turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and roll into a rectangle about 12 inches by 9 inches, with the long side facing you. Try to keep the thickness even, about 1/4 inch. 15. Spread the filling evenly over the dough, leaving a 1/2-inch border along the long top edge bare. 16. Starting from the long edge closest to you, roll the dough up tightly into a log, pinching the seam along the bare edge to seal well. 17. Trim off the uneven ends if needed. Using a sharp knife or unflavored dental floss, cut the log into 12 equal slices, each about 1 inch thick. 18. Take each slice and, with your fingers, gently tuck any loose tail of dough underneath so you have a compact, round spiral. Place each slice cut-side up into a prepared muffin cup, centering it so it touches the bottom and has a little space around the sides. As they rise and bake, they’ll expand to fill the round, flared shape of the wells. 19. Second rise in the pan 20. Cover the filled muffin tin loosely with lightly greased plastic wrap or a clean towel. 21. Let rise in a warm place until the spirals are puffed and nearly fill the cups, about 25–35 minutes. During this rise they’ll settle into the round muffin shape that will hold once baked. 22. Bake 23. Preheat the oven to 350°F. If you have an oven thermometer, check that it actually reads 350°F; adjust as needed. 24. When the spirals are puffed and the dough springs back slowly when gently pressed, place the muffin tin on the center rack. 25. Bake 16–18 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through, until the spiral bites are golden brown on top and the edges where dough meets pan are a deeper golden caramel. The sugar at the bottom will bubble and set, helping the bites hold together. 26. Remove from the oven and set the pan on a wire rack. Let the bites cool in the pan for exactly 5–7 minutes — this allows the caramelized sugar base to firm so each portion unmolds as a cohesive, molded round. 27. Release from the pan 28. After the brief rest, run a thin, offset spatula or butter knife around the inside edge of each cup to loosen the sides, keeping the blade tight against the metal so you don’t tear the roll. 29. Place a baking sheet or large plate over the muffin tin and, holding both together with oven mitts, invert quickly. Lift the muffin tin off; the spiral bites should drop out, each with a lightly caramelized, flat base and rounded, molded sides. 30. If any resist, lift the pan back off, loosen that cup a bit more with the knife, and invert again. Turn each spiral bite right-side up so the spiral faces up on the cooling rack or serving platter. 31. Make the orange-rose glaze 32. In a small bowl, whisk together powdered sugar, 2 tbsp orange juice, orange zest, rose water, melted butter, and a pinch of salt until smooth and pourable. 33. If too thick, whisk in 1/2 tsp more orange juice at a time until it ribbons off the whisk and slowly disappears back into the bowl. If too thin, add 1–2 tbsp more powdered sugar. 34. Glaze and garnish 35. While the spiral bites are still slightly warm but not hot (about 10–15 minutes after unmolding), spoon or drizzle the glaze over the tops, letting it run into the spirals and down the molded sides. 36.
